controls.label: Initial amount N0
controls.help: Sets the starting amount; it scales the remaining amount output and leaves the remaining fraction and half-life unchanged.

controls.label: Decay constant lambda
controls.help: Sets the decay rate; increasing lambda lowers the remaining fraction and remaining amount and shortens the half-life.

controls.label: Time t
controls.help: Sets elapsed time; increasing t lowers the remaining fraction and remaining amount and raises the elapsed half-lives count.

explorations.title: One half-life elapsed
explorations.instruction: Predict: what fraction and amount remain after one half-life? Then apply the preset, which sets N0, lambda and t so that t equals ln(2)/lambda.
explorations.observe: The remaining fraction f readout becomes 0.5, the remaining amount N(t) readout becomes 50, the half-life t_half readout is about 6.93 y, and the elapsed half-lives n_half readout is 1.
explorations.why: When t=ln(2)/lambda, the exponent lambda t equals ln(2), so f=exp(-ln 2)=0.5; multiplying by N0=100 gives N(t)=50.

explorations.title: Faster decay over a shorter time
explorations.instruction: Predict: how do the remaining fraction, remaining amount and half-life change when lambda is larger and t is smaller? Then apply the preset, which sets N0, lambda and t to a fast-decay case.
explorations.observe: The remaining fraction f readout is about 0.368, the remaining amount N(t) readout is about 73.6, the half-life t_half readout is about 1.39 y, and the elapsed half-lives n_half readout is about 1.44.
explorations.why: Here lambda t=1, so f=exp(-1)=0.368; multiplying by N0=200 gives N(t)=73.6. The larger lambda also makes t_half=ln(2)/lambda=1.39 y, so t=2 y spans about 1.44 half-lives.
